commit.message: fix(cli): omit an empty secrets list when updating a deployment (#3414) ## Summary js version of langchain-ai/langgraph#9737. `langgraphjs deploy` builds its secrets list from `.env`, so without one it sent `secrets: []` on every update. the control plane already reads an empty list on update as "keep the current values", so nothing changed, but the request said "replace with nothing". now updates leave `secrets` out when there's nothing to send - the check lives in the two update methods on `HostBackendClient`, so local builds, remote builds and BYOC data planes (which inherit those methods) all get it - creating a deployment still sends `secrets`, even when empty, since the control plane requires it there - no change when your `.env` has variables: the full list is still sent and replaces the deployment's variables as before - patch changeset included ## Test Plan - [x] Format check, lint and `pnpm test` pass in `libs/langgraph-cli` (149 tests). `pnpm typecheck` locally only reports the two existing errors from unbuilt workspace packages, so that's left to CI - [x] New client test: both update methods omit an empty list and send a non-empty one. The remote-build and BYOC local-build deploy tests now also check the update leaves `secrets` out. All fail without the change - [ ] After release, `langgraphjs deploy` without a `.env` against an existing deployment keeps the variables set in the UI ## Demo real cli runs, main vs this branch, against a local server that records each request, with no .env in the project. the control plane handles both requests the same way; the difference is the `secrets` field in the update

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"@langchain/langgraph-cli": patch
+---
+
+`langgraphjs deploy` no longer sends an empty `secrets` list when it updates a deployment and finds no variables to send. The control plane already kept the existing variables in that case; the request now says so explicitly. Creating a deployment still sends `secrets`.
